options.name: Rename existing ZH ## 概述 (Overview) → ## Overview; insert Summary ## 概述; rebuild TOC; re-thread anchors (ZH-side fix, generator's natural path)
options.impl: All work in scripts/gen-package-readme-skeleton.ts. (1) Add a collision-detect+rename helper. In retrofitPair (line 446), the pair plan `pair = extractPairPlan(enRestPre, zhRestPre)` is computed at lines 470-474 from PRE-MUTATION bodies. Add: compute collision indices = { i | pair.zhHeadings[i]==='概述' && pair.enHeadings[i]==='Overview' }. (2) Add renameOverviewCollisions(zhRest, pair) — a line-walk over the ZH body `rest` that, for each collision index in order, rewrites the matching `^## 概述$` line to `## Overview` (only the positionally-correct occurrence; rename in document order via a heading cursor, mirroring insertAnchorsBeforeHeadings' cursor pattern at line 307). (3) Apply the rename to the ZH body BEFORE frontmatter/anchor/skeleton insertion, then RE-DERIVE the pair plan from the renamed ZH rest so pair.zhHeadings and pair.slugs reflect `## Overview` (slug = githubSlug('Overview') = 'overview', matching the EN side). This re-derived plan feeds insertAnchorsBeforeHeadings (line 514) and insertSkeleton (line 518). (4) The hasSummary check (insertSkeleton line 394, `^## 概述$`) now runs against a ZH body whose only remaining `## 概述` would be a Summary the generator inserts — on first run there is none yet, so hasSummary=false → Summary `## 概述` is inserted. On the idempotent second run the inserted Summary makes hasSummary=true → no-op. (5) The tocPairs filter (lines 416-422 excludes words.summary/toc/devNote) now sees the renamed `## Overview` (not excluded) → ZH TOC gains the Overview entry, matching EN's TOC (4 items each). (6) insertAnchorsBeforeHeadings threads `<a id="overview">` before the renamed `## Overview` (matching EN's #overview TOC target); redundant vs GitHub's native `## Overview`→#overview slug but harmless (html nodes are invisible to the pairing signature). Result: EN=[Summary,TOC,Overview,ModelExp,KnownLimitations,DevNote]=6 H2s; ZH=[概述,目录,Overview,ModelExp,KnownLimitations,开发备注]=6 H2s — symmetric. Post-fix wiring (clone gen-tsconfig-paths precedent): package.json add `gen-package-readme-skeleton` (tsx scripts/gen-package-readme-skeleton.ts) + `verify-package-readme-skeleton` (tsx ... --check) near line 139-140; run-gates.ts add `pnpmScript('package-readme-skeleton','verify-package-readme-skeleton',{label:'package README skeleton',quick:true})` near line 758; gate-coverage.manifest.json add the gen- exemption block (script:gen-package-readme-skeleton, reason:'generator (write op, not a gate); its --check variant verify-package-readme-skeleton is enrolled', coveredBy:'verify-package-readme-skeleton gate') near line 74-76. Then run `pnpm run gen-package-readme-skeleton` (writes 130 files), `pnpm run verify-translation-pairing --write <each of 65 pairs>` (re-records 65 README.i18n.yaml sidecars).

options.name: Accept the 16 as manual: generator handles 49 clean pairs; the 16 collision pairs are hand-retrofit in a separate manual pass.
options.impl: All work in scripts/gen-package-readme-skeleton.ts. (1) Add a collision-skip in planRetrofits (line 525) / retrofitPair (line 446). After pair = extractPairPlan (line 470), detect collision (any i with zhHeadings[i]==='概述' && enHeadings[i]==='Overview') and if present, SKIP the pair: either return an empty Retrofit[] from retrofitPair, or return a Retrofit whose current===next so the drift filter (line 537) excludes it. Emit a console warning naming the skipped pair: 'manual retrofit required (ZH 概述/Overview collision) — see UM-FORK-README-SKELETON-RETROFIT'. (2) Run generator for the 49 clean pairs: `pnpm run gen-package-readme-skeleton` writes 98 files (49 pairs), re-record those 49 sidecars. (3) MANUAL pass on the 16: for each, hand-edit (or a one-off uncommitted helper script) to apply EITHER F1-logic (rename ZH 概述→Overview, insert Summary 概述, rebuild TOC, thread anchors) OR F2-logic (rename EN Overview→Summary, keep ZH 概述) per-file. NOTE: F3 does NOT avoid the F1/F2 design decision — the manual pass must still pick one per-file (inserting a Summary `## 概述` alongside the existing Overview `## 概述` would create a duplicate `#概述` slug AND the tocPairs filter would exclude BOTH from the ZH TOC while EN's `## Overview` is included → asymmetry persists). So the manual pass is F1-or-F2 logic done 16× by hand. (4) Wiring: same 4-file clone as F1/F2, BUT verify-package-readme-skeleton --check must SKIP collision pairs (else it reports the 16 as stale forever) — so the --check gate has a documented blind spot for the 16. The doc-standard.spec.ts spec (scans ALL depth-4 files) is the backstop that catches the 16 if they drift.

options.pairingImpact: Keeps all 65 pairs green IF the manual 16-pass is done correctly (it must replicate F1- or F2-logic per-file). But: the manual pass is error-prone (16×2 hand-edits with heading/anchor/TOC threading, no idempotent re-run protection — a second gen run skips the 16 so it cannot self-heal a manual mistake). The generator's --check gate has a blind spot for the 16 (they're skipped), so drift on the 16 is only caught by the heavier doc-standard spec, not the quick freshness gate. F3 does NOT prevent recurrence: every future package with the 概述/Overview shape needs manual handling again unless the generator is later taught F1 or F2. Authored-text change: same as whichever per-file logic (F1's ZH rename or F2's EN rename) is chosen for the manual pass.
options.costEstimate: ~1.5-2 sessions. Generator skip is trivial (~10 lines), but the 16 manual hand-edits (32 files with heading rename + Summary insertion + TOC rebuild + anchor threading + per-pair sidecar re-record) is tedious and unverifiable-by-re-run. Roughly 2× the per-file work of F1 with none of the idempotent safety.

rationale: F1 is the generator's natural fix and is strictly dominant here. Recon confirms every load-bearing fact the prior decision-doc's 'confirm in a grilling session' caveat rested on: (1) The collision is EXACTLY 16 packages — the EN `## Overview` list and the 16-collision list are a perfect 0-discrepancy match (verified via node cross-check), and 0/65 already have `## Summary`, so F1's trigger is precisely bounded and never misfires on the 49 clean packages. (2) The pairing signature (translation-pairing.ts:404 translationStructureSignature pushes node.depth only; translationStructureDiff at :420 compares heading DEPTHS, never text) is INVISIBLE to heading-text changes — so F1's ZH `概述`→`Overview` rename cannot itself break pairing; only the count asymmetry the bug introduces (6 vs 5 H2s) breaks it, and F1 fixes that by ensuring both sides insert the Summary (6 vs 6). (3) F1 is idempotent: on a second run the renamed `## Overview` no longer matches the collision-detect, and the inserted `## 概述` Summary makes hasSummary=true → no-op (verified by logic walk). (4) The authored-ZH-text change (概述→Overview) is evidentially defensible, not a open question: the 16 ZH docs ALREADY render `## Model Experience` and `## Known Limitations and Deferred Work` in English (verified in embedder/audit/query ZH), so English structural headings are the ESTABLISHED convention for these packages — `## Overview` is consistent with their own pattern, and matches the EN side's `## Overview` for cross-language parity. F2 is spec-valid and symmetric but has a real nav regression: it consolidates Overview into Summary and the tocPairs filter (lines 416-422) excludes words.summary from the TOC, so the Overview/Summary becomes unreachable from the TOC on both sides — for packages like embedder where the Overview IS the main contract-definition content, that loses a navigable entry F1 preserves. F3 is strictly weaker than F1: its manual 16-pass must still pick F1- or F2-logic per-file (it does not avoid the design decision), gets no idempotent re-run protection, leaves a --check-gate blind spot, and does not prevent recurrence on new collision-shaped packages. F1 wins on correctness, parity, idempotency, recurrence-prevention, and minimal authored-text disruption. The prior session's F1 recommendation (decision-doc) is CONFIRMED and refined with the exact mechanics + wiring precedent + signature-safety proof + the ZH-English-heading-convention evidence that moots the 'grilling call' concern.
skipJudgePanelIfChosen: Yes — single-agent impl directly. Recon has answered every question a 3-option judge panel would interrogate: exact-16 collision (verified, 0-discrepancy with Overview list), signature-safe rename (pairing compares depths not text), idempotency (logic-walk verified), all-65-green prediction (6v6 H2s / 4v4 TOC / matching links on the 16; 49 untouched), and the authored-text change is evidentially defensible (the 16 ZH docs already use English for Model Experience + Known Limitations headings). The only residual is a lightweight human nod on the ZH 概述→Overview text change — but that is now evidence-backed, not an open design question.
